decisions.title: Definition of "legacy paths" for the SPS2 legacy-protection controls
decisions.decision: TERM DEFINITION ONLY, AND PROPOSED ONLY - NOT AN APPROVED RULE. For the purposes of the SPS2 legacy-protection controls, "legacy paths" means the following paths and no others: the directories skills/, scripts/, plugins/, .github/, templates/, and .sps/tools/; the files README.md, CHANGELOG.md and CATALOG.md; and the installer scripts install.sh, install.ps1, uninstall.sh, uninstall.ps1, get-sps.sh and get-sps.ps1. This definition deliberately names .sps/tools/ rather than .sps/ wholesale: measured against the current working tree, enumerating .sps/ would cover nine paths instead of three, sweeping in six unrelated governance files whose protection status remains undecided - .sps/architecture/SPS2-ROADMAP.md, .sps/audits/README.md, .sps/changelog-sps.md, .sps/handoff.md, .sps/p17/real-agent-execution.json and .sps/plan.md - and this record makes no determination about any of them, including whether .sps/audits/README.md is protected. This definition also names the six installer scripts explicitly because the directory list alone reaches none of them: omitting them would drop prospective protection for nine files, six of which are real legacy installers that REQ-P1-06 explicitly treats as legacy. This record DEFINES A TERM ONLY. It changes no file: no validator, no pathspec, no control behaviour, no acceptance criterion, no requirement text, no approval state and no verification state is modified; it creates and modifies no requirement; and it makes no validator pass. REQ-P3-08's criterion text, its APPROVED status and its VERIFIED verification state are UNCHANGED, and its implementation continues to use its current pathspec. DEC-0028 remains in force and nothing here weakens the P3/P4 legacy-protection controls. DEC-0029 remains PROPOSED and is not contradicted or relied upon as authorization; this definition is consistent with that record's scope direction. Normative tension, stated honestly: this record does NOT claim that defining the term outside REQ-P3-08 is unambiguously permitted. DEC-0028 records that 'legacy paths' is currently defined operatively only by the script pathspecs and warns that redefining the meaning of an approved and verified criterion is a normative change. Defining the term in this record therefore raises a genuine normative question. This record does not resolve that question, does not settle it in its own favour, and does not authorize any implementation. Until this proposal is explicitly approved by the User, the definition above must NOT be treated as an approved governance rule, and it must not be cited as authority to change any validator or pathspec. Changing a validator's pathspec to match this definition is a SEPARATE decision, is NOT taken here, and would require its own explicit authorization. UQ-ATT-1 is NOT resolved by this record: the remaining enumeration/implementation question stays OPEN.
decisions.reason: The term "legacy paths" is defined in no approved artifact. It exists operatively only in validator script pathspecs, and those pathspecs disagree about its extent. Measured against the current working tree: the three controls at sps2/tools/validate-p2.sh:194, sps2/tools/validate-p3.sh:297-299 and sps2/tools/validate-p4.sh:482-484 use the identical pathspec 'skills scripts plugins .github templates README.md CHANGELOG.md CATALOG.md *.sh *.ps1' piped through grep -v '^sps2/', and the unanchored '*.sh'/'*.ps1' glob reaches .sps/tools/ at any depth, so they currently report exactly three modified legacy governance files; the two controls at sps2/tools/validate-sps2.sh:198-199 and sps2/tools/validate-p5.py:281-283 use glob-free explicit enumerations and currently report an empty diff. The directory list alone provably cannot reach .sps/ at all, so the glob is the sole cause of the divergence. The unanchored glob is also wider than the stated legacy intent, because it additionally covers three repo-root files that .sps/audits/README.md:45 classifies as orphan debug artifacts (KI-05) rather than legacy files. REQ-P1-06's approved criterion refers to "installers", which matches an explicit list rather than a shell glob. DEC-0028 recorded explicit enumeration as the correct long-term remedy, called it the minimum outstanding decision, and identified the undefined term as the reason the current pathspec cannot be narrowed unilaterally. Recording the definition disambiguates the term without editing an approved requirement, which requirement.schema.json provides no mechanism to amend because it sets additionalProperties false and has no amendment, version or supersession field. The definition is deliberately behaviour-preserving against the current working tree: measured with the current tree it flags exactly the same three .sps/tools/ validator files as the status-quo glob. This record is PROPOSED rather than ACTIVE because the normative tension above is real and requires a distinct User approval before the definition can be relied upon as a governance rule.
evidence: sps2/governance/SCHEMAS/decision.schema.json defines $id sps2/decision/v1, requires decision_id, title, decision, reason, evidence, alternatives and approval, sets additionalProperties false at the top level and inside approval, defines evidence as an array of strings with minItems 1, defines alternatives as an array of objects, requires only state inside approval, and defines supersedes as string or null; it provides no amendment or version field

sps2/governance/SCHEMAS/requirement.schema.json sets additionalProperties false and its properties are acceptance_criteria, approval, dependencies, description, evidence_refs, implementation, objective, requirement_id, risk, scope, status, title and verification; it contains no amendment, version, supersedes, revision or history property, so the acceptance criterion text of an approved requirement cannot be amended in place without violating the schema

Measured: git diff --name-only c11da27 -- '*.sh' '*.ps1' filtered by grep -v '^sps2/' yields exactly .sps/tools/validate-capability.sh, .sps/tools/validate-control.sh and .sps/tools/validate-governance.sh, a count of 3

Measured: the full definition recorded here, evaluated against the current working tree as 'git diff --name-only c11da27 -- skills scripts plugins .github templates README.md CHANGELOG.md CATALOG.md install.sh install.ps1 uninstall.sh uninstall.ps1 get-sps.sh get-sps.ps1 .sps/tools', yields exactly 3 files, the same .sps/tools/ validators as the status-quo glob, so the definition is behaviour-preserving today

Measured: of 38 tracked .sh and .ps1 files at c11da27, none are under sps2/. Omitting the six installer scripts from the definition would drop prospective protection for nine files: get-sps.sh, get-sps.ps1, install.sh, install.ps1, uninstall.sh, uninstall.ps1, test_claude.sh, test_timeout.sh and test_uiux.sh; naming the six installers reduces that residual to exactly three

alternatives.option: Leave the term undefined and keep the status-quo unanchored glob pathspecs unchanged
alternatives.why_not_chosen: It preserves the ambiguity DEC-0028 identified as the reason the pathspec cannot be narrowed unilaterally, and the glob is provably wider than the stated legacy intent because it also covers three KI-05 orphan debug artifacts. It remains the only option that changes nothing whatsoever, and it stays available if the User prefers the term to remain undefined.

alternatives.option: Define "legacy paths" by enumerating .sps/ wholesale rather than .sps/tools/
alternatives.why_not_chosen: Measured, it would cover 9 paths instead of 3, sweeping in six unrelated governance files whose protection status is undecided: .sps/architecture/SPS2-ROADMAP.md, .sps/audits/README.md, .sps/changelog-sps.md, .sps/handoff.md, .sps/p17/real-agent-execution.json and .sps/plan.md. It would also appear to decide the .sps/audits/README.md question that this record deliberately leaves open.

alternatives.option: Define "legacy paths" using the directory list only, without naming the installer scripts
alternatives.why_not_chosen: Measured, it would drop prospective protection for nine files, six of which are real legacy installer scripts that REQ-P1-06 explicitly treats as legacy: install.sh, install.ps1, uninstall.sh, uninstall.ps1, get-sps.sh and get-sps.ps1. Naming them is required for the definition to be faithful to the approved criterion's wording.

alternatives.option: Amend REQ-P3-08's acceptance criterion to enumerate the paths in place
alternatives.why_not_chosen: requirement.schema.json sets additionalProperties false and provides no amendment, version or supersession mechanism, so the criterion text cannot be amended without violating the schema, and .sps/GOVERNANCE.md directs that history not be silently edited. DEC-0028 also recorded that amending an approved requirement's acceptance criteria is not authorised by its instruction.

alternatives.option: Treat this record as authorizing the validators' pathspecs to be changed to match the definition
alternatives.why_not_chosen: Expressly not taken here. The envelopes of ATTRIBUTION-POLICY-DECISIONS.json and LEGACY-SCOPE-DECISIONS.json bar changes to REQ-P3-08 and to validator, pathspec or control behaviour, and any narrowing that excludes .sps/tools/. Changing a pathspec would require separate explicit authorization, and this record is not that authorization.

alternatives.option: Create this record as ACTIVE and treat the definition as an approved governance rule immediately
alternatives.why_not_chosen: It would fabricate approval. DEC-0028 states that the term is currently defined operatively only by the script pathspecs and that redefining the meaning of an approved and verified criterion is a normative change; that tension is real and unresolved. Treating the definition as approved without explicit User approval would misrepresent the governance state, so this record is PROPOSED with approval.state PENDING_USER_APPROVAL and states that the definition must not be relied upon as a rule until the User approves it.

alternatives.option: Assert in this record that defining the term is unambiguously permitted because it changes no file
alternatives.why_not_chosen: The position is genuinely two-sided and must not be overstated. Every existing bar is worded by effect, and a definition changes no file, byte, behaviour or state, which supports treating it as outside those bars. But DEC-0028 states the term is defined only in the script pathspec, which makes the pathspec the sole operative definition in force, so defining the term elsewhere can equally be read as the same normative move DEC-0028 called outside its authorization. This record therefore states the tension explicitly and depends on a distinct User approval rather than claiming the question is settled.
